name: White vertices are symmetric
summary: Swapping two legs of a white vertex (Z-box) gives the same white vertex.
description: The (labelled) white vertices of the ZW-calculus, $|0\cdots0\rangle + r\,|1\cdots1\rangle$, are symmetric: swapping two of their legs with an ordinary swap does not change them. In the 2015 paper (Rule 0) the white vertices are unlabelled Z-spiders with phase $\pi$; in the thesis ($sym_z$) and in Hadzihasanovic, Ng and Wang (3(c)) they carry a label $r$ from a commutative ring. In PyZX this holds by construction.
parameter_notes: Shown for a white vertex with four legs; holds for any number of legs.
unchecked_reason: both sides are the same PyZX graph: symmetry of the generator is built into the graph representation

also_in.location: Chapter 5, Section 5.2 (list of rules of the ZW calculus), rule $sym_z$
